tweets.text:
On the margins of the 4th UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence in Riyadh yesterday, our UN Country Team had a useful conversation about what AI is already changing across our work.

The discussion moved quickly from technology to people. From anticipating where hunger may deepen, to planning cities, tourism, migration and labour markets, the possibilities are significant. But each conversation brought us back to similar questions: how we protect people's data, how we identify unintended harm, and how we bring our different areas of expertise together in a way that is useful to governments.

None of us has all the answers. But across the UN system, we have accumulated experience from working through many of the underlying questions that AI is now reshaping, in classrooms, clinics, farms, cities and workplaces around the world.

It is fitting that this conversation took place here. Saudi Arabia is advancing its AI agenda at remarkable pace, and in its Year of Artificial Intelligence it has welcomed this Forum to the Arab region for the first time. As the Kingdom sets that pace, our role is to listen, to learn, and to bring what we know together, as one UN, wherever it can be useful to the Kingdom's institutions and to the priorities of Vision 2030.

My thanks to Salah Khaled and the UNESCO team for convening our discussion, and to SDAIA and ICAIRE for bringing the Forum to Riyadh.

#GFEAI2026 #EthicsOfAI #SaudiArabia #Vision2030 #UNinKSA @UNESCO_GCCYemen

The Namibian Parliament is attending the 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference in Cape Town, South Africa, where lawmakers and parliamentary officials from across the Commonwealth are discussing parliamentary democracy, good governance and institutional development.

The conference, which runs from 13 to 18 September, is also addressing inclusive and fair trade, inequality and underdevelopment, climate adaptation and resilience, the use of artificial intelligence in parliaments, human rights and the promotion of peace.

The delegation is led by National Council Chairperson Lukas Muha and includes Raymond Jossop and Christopher Likuwa, as well as the Secretaries of the two Houses, Adv. Tousy Namiseb and Esther Kaapanda.

Muha is participating in meetings of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association International Executive Committee, where he serves as the Southern African Regional Representative.

His participation allows Namibia to contribute to discussions and decisions shaping the work and strategic direction of the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association.

Namiseb and Kaapanda are expected to participate in the 69th General Meeting of the Society of Clerks at the Table, which brings together senior parliamentary officials to exchange experiences and best practices on the administration and functioning of legislatures across the Commonwealth.

The conference provides a platform for the delegation to share parliamentary experiences, strengthen inter-parliamentary relations and contribute to discussions on emerging challenges facing legislatures and democratic institutions.

Report: Serafia Nadunya

Senator Salisu Hails FUNAAB’s Role in Youth Empowerment, Job Creation

 … As the 16th Annual Conference of MYCOSON Begins on Campus

By Olasunkanmi Olajide

The Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta (FUNAAB) has been commended for its strategic role in youth empowerment, job creation and human-capital development, particularly through education, agriculture and skills development.

The Chairman, Senate Committee on ICT and Cybersecurity, Senator Shuaib Afolabi Salisu, gave the commendation on September 14, 2026, at the Opening Ceremony of the 16th Annual Conference of the Mycology Society of Nigeria (MYCOSON), tagged MYCOSON-FUNAAB 2026, in FUNAAB.

Themed “Integrating Fungal Biotechnology with Digital Innovation for Agricultural and Industrial Developments in Nigeria,” the distinguished Senator who represents Ogun Central Senatorial District, described FUNAAB as a strategic partner in advancing his major interests in education, job placement and youth development, declaring that the University had become “part of my DNA”.

The Senator specifically commended FUNAAB for its sustained contribution to equipping young Nigerians with relevant agricultural skills and creating pathways for employment and economic empowerment.

“Whenever I want to train our youth in agriculture, you have continued to provide the manpower to train them and provide them resources. You provide them the intellectual skills that they require to do the job,” he said.

He expressed appreciation to the University for its contribution to human-capital development and pledged continued collaboration in areas capable of advancing education, youth empowerment, employment and national development.

Earlier in his Opening Remarks, the Vice-Chancellor, FUNAAB, Prof. Babatunde Kehinde, congratulated MYCOSON on convening the conference, expressing confidence that the calibre of participants and the quality of preparations had positioned the event for success.

Prof. Kehinde noted that the University’s strong academic and research tradition would provide a fertile ground for discussions capable of generating practical, home-grown solutions to challenges confronting Nigeria’s agricultural sector.

The National President of MYCOSON, Prof. Raphael Okigbo, appreciated the Vice-Chancellor and the University for hosting the conference, while urging participants to use the technical sessions to freely share their research findings, practical experiences and innovative ideas.

Also speaking, Chairperson of the Local Organising Committee and the Dean, College of Biosciences (COLBIOS), Prof. Iyabode Kehinde, encouraged participants to explore FUNAAB’s serene and green environment during the conference.

She particularly urged Undergraduate and Postgraduate students attending the conference to maximise the opportunity by registering as members of the Society and building professional networks with researchers and practitioners in Mycology.

The first Keynote Address was delivered by the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Federal University of Agriculture and Development Studies (FUADSI), Prof. Charles Adetunji, who spoke on the title “From Laboratory to Marketplace: Fungal Biotechnology and Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Agriculture Transformation, Food Security and National Development.”

The second Keynote Speaker, Prof. Adewale Obadina, Quality Assurance and Accreditation Officer, Association of African Universities (AAU), Accra, Ghana, spoke on “Harnessing Fungal Resources for Food Security and Commercial Value Creation in Emerging Economies.”
